Choosing a results generator

Saiem Gilani

Source: vignettes/results-generators.Rmd
results-generators.Rmd

cfb_simulations() fills every unplayed game with a compute_results function. cfbseedR ships two:

Generator Driven by Ratings during the season Defaults fitted on
cfbseedR_compute_results() (default) a dynamic ELO rating updated every week from the (real or simulated) results FBS-vs-FBS games 2014-2025
cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results() fixed team ratings you supply: points, adjusted EPA/play or raw EPA/play fixed FBS-vs-FBS games 2014-2025, walk-forward

This article shows both on the bundled toy season, offline. The companion article Ratings and EPA inputs builds real ratings from cfbfastR and reports how each generator scored on real seasons.

library(cfbseedR)

games <- cfb_games_example
teams <- cfb_teams_example
games$result[games$week >= 3] <- NA

Which one to use

Use the default ELO generator unless you have a reason not to. In a walk-forward test on 2014-2025 (2020 left out), the ELO margin formula fed with CollegeFootballData’s pregame ELO had the smallest error overall: a mean absolute error of 12.94 points, against 13.10 for a current-season least-squares points rating and 13.38 / 13.70 for the fitting script’s adjusted / raw EPA ratings. Its edge is early in the season: that ELO carries over from the previous season, while a current-season rating starts from nothing. To get the same from the simulator, pass carried-over ratings as elo (below); without them every team starts from a random rating.

Use a points rating late in the season or for the postseason. Once both teams have about six games, the points rating is level with ELO: with 8 or more games behind the weaker rating its error was 12.93 against ELO’s 13.04, a difference within the test’s noise. If you are simulating the last weeks of a season, or the bowls and the playoff, from current ratings, it is a sound input. The test used its own least-squares rating; published ratings such as SP+ or FPI are on the same points scale and work the same way, but they were not part of it.

The EPA ratings are there as options. They need play-by-play data, and the script’s versions trailed the points rating at every stage of the season.

The default: ELO

The ELO generator needs nothing but the schedule. It starts every team at a random rating unless you pass elo, a named vector of starting ratings:

elo <- setNames(seq(1700, 1300, length.out = nrow(teams)), teams$team)
set.seed(1)
sim_elo <- cfb_simulations(
  games, teams,
  simulations = 20, playoff_seeds = 4, elo = elo, verbosity = "NONE"
)
sim_elo$overall[, c("team", "wins", "conf_champ", "playoff")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   team   wins conf_champ playoff
#>   <chr> <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 A1     2.95       0.55    0.6 
#> 2 A2     1.85       0.45    0.45
#> 3 A3     2.6        0       1   
#> 4 A4     1.1        0       0   
#> 5 B1     3.55       0.6     0.85
#> 6 B2     2          0.4     0.5 
#> 7 B3     1.25       0       0.25
#> 8 B4     0.9        0       0.15
#> 9 I1     0.8        0       0.2

Its home_field (59.4 ELO points, 2.38 points of margin) and margin_sd (16.7 points) can be overridden through cfb_simulations()’s ....

Fixed ratings: cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results()

The ratings generator takes a data frame with team, rating and, optionally, games (how many games are behind each rating), and a rating_type that picks the defaults:

ratings <- data.frame(
  team = teams$team,
  rating = seq(12, -12, length.out = nrow(teams)), # points per game
  games = 8
)
simulations_verify_fct(
  cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results,
  ratings = ratings, rating_type = "points"
)

set.seed(1)
sim_pts <- cfb_simulations(
  games, teams,
  compute_results = cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results,
  ratings = ratings, rating_type = "points",
  simulations = 20, playoff_seeds = 4, verbosity = "NONE"
)
sim_pts$overall[, c("team", "wins", "conf_champ", "playoff")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 4
#>   team   wins conf_champ playoff
#>   <chr> <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 A1     3.15        0.6    0.7 
#> 2 A2     1.85        0.4    0.45
#> 3 A3     2.55        0      1   
#> 4 A4     1.05        0      0.05
#> 5 B1     3.65        0.6    0.9 
#> 6 B2     2           0.4    0.55
#> 7 B3     1.15        0      0.15
#> 8 B4     1           0      0.1 
#> 9 I1     0.6         0      0.1

The expected home margin of a game is scale * (rating_home - rating_away) + home_field (no home_field at a neutral site), and the simulated margin is a normal draw around it with standard deviation margin_sd, rounded away from zero. The ratings do not move during the simulation.

The three rating types

rating_type Rating scale (points per rating unit) margin_sd home_field
"points" points per game (SP+, FPI, a margin rating) 1.09 / 0.92 / 1.03 / 1.06 16.97 / 16.64 / 16.23 / 16.45 2.38
"adj_epa" opponent-adjusted net EPA per play 31.9 / 37.9 / 45.2 / 49.6 17.04 2.76
"raw_epa" net EPA per play, no adjustment 28.6 / 34.3 / 45.1 / 52.0 17.93 / 17.24 / 16.98 / 17.39 2.38

Values are by the games played behind the weaker of the two ratings: 0-3, 4-5, 6-7 and 8-20 games. An EPA rating built on two games predicts less well than one built on ten, so its points-per-unit scale is smaller: a 0.1 raw EPA/play edge is worth about 2.9 points with three games behind it and 5.2 points with ten (3.2 and 5.0 for adjusted EPA). The points scale stays close to 1 throughout. With the noise switched off (margin_sd = 0) the simulated margin is just the rounded expected margin, which shows the effect:

epa <- data.frame(team = c("A", "B"), rating = c(0.1, 0))
one_game <- data.frame(
  sim = 1, week = 1, game_type = "REG", home_team = "A", away_team = "B",
  result = NA_integer_, neutral = 1
)
two_teams <- data.frame(sim = 1, team = c("A", "B"), conference = "X")
sapply(c(early = 3, late = 10), function(n) {
  cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results(
    two_teams, one_game, 1,
    ratings = transform(epa, games = n), rating_type = "raw_epa", margin_sd = 0
  )$games$result
})
#> early  late 
#>     3     6

Without a games column every game uses the top bucket, which treats the ratings as full-season ratings. Early in a season that overstates how much an EPA rating is worth, so pass games when you have it.

Your own constants

scale, home_field and margin_sd accept your own values: one number, or a named vector of "lo-hi" games-played buckets.

set.seed(3)
sim_custom <- cfb_simulations(
  games, teams,
  compute_results = cfbseedR_ratings_compute_results,
  ratings = ratings[c("team", "rating")],
  scale = 1, home_field = 2.5, margin_sd = 16,
  simulations = 20, playoff_seeds = 4, verbosity = "NONE"
)
sim_custom$overall[, c("team", "wins", "playoff")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 3
#>   team   wins playoff
#>   <chr> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 A1     3.35    0.95
#> 2 A2     2.1     0.35
#> 3 A3     2.4     1   
#> 4 A4     0.9     0.1 
#> 5 B1     3.35    0.85
#> 6 B2     2       0.35
#> 7 B3     1.3     0.3 
#> 8 B4     1       0.05
#> 9 I1     0.6     0.05

Pass your own scale and margin_sd whenever your rating is on a different scale from the defaults. The "adj_epa" defaults are sportsdataverse-py’s pregame-prediction constants, fitted to that package’s adj_net, so a rating from another opponent adjustment may need its own values.

Teams without a rating

A team missing from ratings (an FCS opponent, say) gets a rating of 0, league average. For FBS ratings that flatters an FCS team, so give such teams an explicit low rating if their games matter to you.
